Table theme

Source: R/table.R
pub_table_theme.Rd

The styling that pub_table() applies when it builds or finishes a table: font size, borders, number format and other cell properties. To use a theme for all tables, set it as default with options(pubflow.table_theme = pub_table_theme(...)).

Usage

pub_table_theme(
  ...,
  font_size = 9,
  borders = c("booktabs", "grid"),
  number_format = 4L
)

Arguments

...

Further huxtable cell properties applied to every cell, e.g. font = "Arial" or top_padding = 2 (see huxtable::style_cells()).

font_size

Font size in points.

borders

"booktabs": horizontal rules above and below the header (and below spanners) and below the body; "grid": borders around all header and body cells.

number_format

Format of numeric (non-integer) columns without digits (integer columns get 0 decimal places), one of

  • a whole number of decimal places;

  • a sprintf() format with one %.nf, %.ne or %.ng conversion;

  • a function returning one string per value;

  • NA: as.character().

See pub_cell_text().

Value

An object of class pub_table_theme.

Details

The arguments after ... must be named in full, so that font = "Arial" reaches huxtable instead of being taken for font_size.

See also

pub_table()

Examples

theme <- pub_table_theme(font_size = 8, borders = "grid", font = "Arial")
ht <- pub_table(data.frame(x = c(1.5, 2)), theme = theme)
pub_cell_text(ht)
#>      [,1]    
#> [1,] "x"     
#> [2,] "1.5000"
#> [3,] "2.0000"
huxtable::font(ht)[1, 1]
#> [1] "Arial"

pub_table(data.frame(x = 1 / 3), theme = pub_table_theme(
    number_format = "%.2e"
)) |>
    pub_cell_text()
#>      [,1]      
#> [1,] "x"       
#> [2,] "3.33e-01"
